title: Health and readiness endpoints
when: A Node service runs behind a process manager, load balancer or container orchestrator and needs endpoints saying whether it is alive and whether it can take traffic.
inputs: dependencies such as database and storage
prompt:
Goal: GET /healthz for liveness and GET /readyz for readiness: cheap, unauthenticated and honest about dependencies.
Steps:
1. /healthz replies 200 { "status": "ok" } while the event loop runs; it checks nothing external, so a slow database causes no restarts.
2. /readyz runs quick checks with about 1 s timeout each: SELECT 1, storage folder writable, migrations applied, queue not stuck.
3. Reply 200 { "status": "ready", "checks": { "db": "ok" } } or 503 { "status": "not_ready", "checks": { "db": "timeout" } }.
4. /readyz says 503 during startup until migrations finish and from the moment shutdown begins.
5. Cache readiness for a few seconds so frequent probes do not load the database.
6. Send Cache-Control: no-store, keep probes out of access logs, and exempt them from rate limits.
Quality bar:
- Public replies reveal no versions, hostnames or error text; details only on an internal port.
- Worst case probe time is under 2 s.
- Probe paths and codes are documented.
Pitfalls:
- Liveness tied to the database, causing restart loops in an outage.
- Readiness that always says 200.
- Heavy queries inside probes.
Verify:
- [ ] /healthz touches no dependency.
- [ ] A test closes the database and gets 503 from /readyz.
- [ ] Shutdown flips readiness to 503.
- [ ] Probes send no-store.
Output: routes/health.mjs, a probe section in README.md, test/health.test.mjs.

examples.input: add health checks for the load balancer
examples.output: /healthz always cheap, /readyz checks db and storage with timeouts, 503 during startup and shutdown
